context:
2026-11-06: Delete the two archived probe repositories created on 2026-11-04 to prove that `secrets: inherit` does not cross owners: joeharris76/secrets-probe-callee and the secrets-probe-caller repository (in the BenchBox-dev organization). Agents' gh token lacks the delete_repo scope. Run `gh auth refresh -s delete_repo`, then `gh repo delete <owner>/<name> --yes` for each. The finding they proved is recorded on oracle-callers-env-secrets-unreachable-20261104, so nothing else depends on them.

2026-11-07 owner action: report the TPC-DS kit refresh-key bug to the TPC. In tools/scaling.c, getUpdateBase() reads arRowcount[nTable - S_BRAND] while setUpdateScaling() writes arRowcount[nTable], so refresh order and ticket ids restart at 1 and overlap the base keys at every scale. Evidence is in tpcds-maintenance-dsdgen-refresh-data-20261103 and docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md (K9).

2026-11-09 correction to the 2026-11-07 TPC-DS kit entry above: reporting the refresh-key bug upstream is OPTIONAL, not a required step. BenchBox already handles it: maintenance refuses when primary keys are enforced, and the deviation is documented as K9 in docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md. The mechanism is verified in public source (gregrahn/tpcds-kit: getUpdateBase reads arRowcount[nTable - S_BRAND], an unrelated zero slot, while setUpdateScaling writes arRowcount[nTable]; the - S_BRAND offset belongs to the separate s_tdef_funcs array, see tdef_functions.c:176-177). The official TPC-DS 4.0.0 source was not read; for 4.0.0 the evidence is the bundled binary producing refresh ids from 1. Options if you want it reported: a TPC bug report (needs a TPC account), or a public issue on gregrahn/tpcds-kit (third-party publication; needs owner OK).

work_units.notes:
Source: rename-release-branch-main-to-release (w5/w6, ADMIN half).
w3 below (branch-default-switch-to-develop) is DONE, so this is now only
blocked on w1. Run RIGHT AFTER w1 merges, per
docs/operations/branch-rename-runbook.md:
  gh api -X POST repos/joeharris76/BenchBox/branches/main/rename -f new_name=release
Then recreate the `main-release-only` ruleset as `release-only` targeting
refs/heads/release (same required checks/protections), and update the
ruleset-id reference in docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md.
No real coverage gap exists because the release branch only receives pushes
via release-cut/release-finalize (both maintainer-controlled); if
`make release-cut` is run before the rename it fails fast (base does not
exist) rather than mis-cutting.
